newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends up 18 cts in late rally after slump.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends up 18 cts in late rally after slump.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures settled 18 cents firmer on Monday in a technically-driven recovery after revisiting six-month lows for the second straight trading day, traders said.

The March Brent contract last traded at $21.11 a barrel after crashing through several support levels to a low of $20.55 in mid-afternoon in sympathy with heavy selling on the NYMEX unleaded gasoline contract.
"Chartists decided it was time for a change after several days of new lows," a trader said.
Later gains on NYMEX heating oil and gasoline broke Brent's fall and provided the platform for the chartists' rapid upside break in the final 40 minutes of business, they added.
"Brent was so oversold it (the rally) doesn't make much difference. If Brent goes much further above $21 tomorrow it'll be quickly sold into," a trader added.
March Brent closed at $20.95 on Friday in a sharp selloff which push the spot contract below $21 for the first time since August.

IPE gas oil closed $2 a tonne lower on Monday, but off earlier lows on NYMEX gasoline's recovery. Feb gas oil, which expires on Wednesday, closed $2 lower at $188.25 a tonne, having dipped to a session low of $186.25. March shed $4, widening the front month backwardation to $7 a tonne.
